x: They were then lost to sight whilst a lap of some 6 miles was traversed, and when again seen, the field was headed by Sandy, Surrey A.C., with Vickers, Sheffield, in close attendance. Then came Plumb, N.L H., Reddish, H.H.H., and Ludlow, Derby W.C.
At Croydon the field was led by Heaney, of Lancashire Walking Club, with a group consisting of Green, Lloyd-Johnson (Leicester), Ludlow and Taylor (Derby W.C.), D.

This reduced our number of starters to seven, and it was evident from the start that our walkers intended playing an important part in the race. At Croydon, Green and Rickards of ours, Ludlow (Derby W. & A.C.) and D. Gum (Essex Eagles) were leading the field.
At the G.P.O., Redhill (20¼ miles) Green's time was 3 hrs. 1 min. 17 secs., 3 minutes inside Ludlow's time of last year when the record was created; and everything was very rosy!
Even at this early stage it was evident that Ludlow's record was in danger. At the "Chequers," Horley, approaching half-distance, Whitlock had a good lead, about three minutes inside record.
Two Miles: 1 Walker (N.); 2 Ludlow; 3 Tobin. 10 mins. 28.4 secs. Two Miles' Walk: 1 Martin (D.). 2 McMullen; 3 Rouse; 4 Speechley; 5 Wilson. 15 mins. 17 secs.
For purposes of comparison we have given calculated times for speeds varying from 5½ to 6¾ mph together with the actual times of the Green - Ludlow - H.Whitlock record holders of pre-war days.

He completed a hat-trick of victories the following two years and then lost out in 1932 after a terrific struggle with Ludlow of Derby, the latter breaking the course record set by Tommy in 1930 with 8hrs. 2mins. 55secs.
